claim: Apprise can send notifications to both ntfy (ntfy://topic/) and Gotify (gotify://hostname/token or gotifys://), positioning it as a dispatch layer that targets ntfy/Gotify rather than competing with them.
quote: gotify:// or gotifys:// ... gotify://hostname/token ... ntfy:// ... Apprise allows you to send a notification to almost all of the most popular notification services available to us today such as: Telegram, Discord, Slack, Amazon SNS, Gotify, etc.

claim: Home Assistant's Apprise integration binds to the notify.NAME action and connects to more than 140 notification services configured via Apprise URLs.
quote: The notifier will bind to the action notify.NAME ... more than 140 notification services ... Add one or more Apprise URLs directly to your configuration.

claim: Home Assistant ships a native core ntfy integration (added in 2025.05) that adds a device and sensors for account usage and subscribes to topics, separate from the Apprise route.
quote: The ntfy integration adds a device representing the service, along with various sensors that display your usage statistics and current account limits.

claim: Watchtower sends notifications through shoutrrr via WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL, with legacy shorthand backends for Gotify (WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL/TOKEN).
quote: --notification-url (env. WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL): The shoutrrr service URL to be used ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=gotify ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TOKEN

claim: Watchtower can push to ntfy via a shoutrrr generic/ntfy URL, e.g. ntfy://ntfy.sh/your-topic, configured through WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL.
quote: You can use shoutrrr to send Watchtower notifications to your ntfy topic ... ntfy://ntfy.sh/your-ntfy-channel ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=shoutrrr

claim: ntfy lists native integrations across the homelab stack: Home Assistant, Uptime Kuma, Watchtower, Healthchecks, Gatus, plus Grafana bridges and Apprise as a universal notification bridge that includes ntfy as a target.
quote: Home Assistant ... Uptime Kuma ... Watchtower ... Healthchecks.io ... Gatus ... Apprise serves as a universal notification bridge ... includes ntfy as one of its supported services

claim: Grafana alerting reaches ntfy through its generic Webhook contact point, which POSTs a JSON payload with a customizable Custom Payload template to any URL.
quote: The webhook integration is a flexible way to integrate alerts into your system. When a notification is triggered, it sends a JSON request with alert details and additional data to the webhook endpoint.

claim: A dedicated bridge (grafana-alerting-ntfy-webhook-integration) runs a small HTTP server that reformats Grafana's alerting webhook JSON into ntfy's format, easing the Grafana to ntfy path.
quote: Integration between https://ntfy.sh/ and grafana alerting ... a small simple http server that takes a grafana alerting json webhook and re-formats it for ntfy format

claim: Apprise is positioned as a notification aggregator/dispatch layer fronting services like ntfy and Gotify, letting one call fan out to many destinations including file/attachment delivery that plain ntfy or Gotify push lacks.
quote: Apprise is a notification aggregator that supports 80+ services: Discord, Telegram, Slack, email, Ntfy, Gotify, Pushover ... Apprise's ability to send files to supported services is powerful

claim: A common architectural pattern is one webhook into Apprise which then routes simultaneously to multiple destinations (ntfy, Gotify, email, chat), with ntfy/Gotify acting as the delivery+app endpoints.
quote: you can send one webhook from Jellyfin -> Apprise routes it to multiple destinations simultaneously

claim: Uptime Kuma offers native notification providers for Gotify (and 90+ services including ntfy and Apprise), selectable directly in its Settings > Notifications UI.
quote: Notifications via Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, Email (SMTP), and 90+ notification services, click here for the full list
